# Adjudication Task — Chapter 263

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃263화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“그것도 가장 소중한 벗을 죽인 원수지.”
  6|
  7|그 한마디에 나는 우뚝 굳었다. 옆에 있는 적천강의 머릿속에도 나와 같은 생각이 떠올랐을 것이다.
  8|
  9|‘지금 무슨 소리를 들은 거지?’
 10|
 11|순간 이해가 되지 않았다. 낯선 얼굴을 한 청년의 입에서 나온 말에 머릿속이 뒤죽박죽 엉켜 들었다.
 12|
 13|지금 그러니까…….
 14|
 15|‘굉도를 죽였다고? 저놈이?’
 16|
 17|뇌리 깊숙이 각인된 기억들이 눈앞에 떠올랐다가 사라진다.
 18|
 19|비무 도중 사라진 종리추와 죽음의 문턱에서 헐떡거리던 굉도, 그리고 그가 유언으로 남긴 네 개의 단어.
 20|
 21|‘종리추, 암천, 무명, 불장.’
 22|
 23|지금까지 내가 보고 들은 그것들은 도대체 무엇이었을까.
 24|
 25|도대체 어디서, 어떻게 흘러간 것일까.
 26|
 27|나는 석상처럼 굳은 채 실마리를 잡으려 애썼지만, 생각을 잇기도 전에 적천강의 입술 사이로 메마른 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 28|
 29|“네놈이, 굉도를, 죽였다고?”
 30|
 31|뚝뚝 끊기는 목소리는 인내와 분노, 그리고 불신으로 젖어 있었다. 그런 적천강의 모습에 청년이 잔잔하게 웃으며 고개를 끄덕였다.
 32|
 33|“그렇다니까. 생각보다 훨씬 쉬웠어. 관중석에 진천뢰(振天雷)를 터트리겠다고 하니 순순히 따라오더군.”
 34|
 35|“진천뢰? 폭약을 심어 뒀었나?”
 36|
 37|“아, 그거? 당연히 거짓말이었는데.”
 38|
 39|“……뭐라?”
 40|
 41|“사람들이 거짓말을 하는 이유가 뭐겠나? 가끔 속는 멍청한 놈들이 있기 때문이지.”
 42|
 43|으스러져라 움켜쥔 적천강의 주먹에서 핏방울이 뚝뚝 떨어졌다.
 44|
 45|“속은 것이 아니라 속아 준 것이다. 굉도는 그런 사람이니까.”
 46|
 47|“속아 줬다? 뭐 그럴 수도 있겠군. 소림사 방장씩이나 되는 땡중이니 혹시 모를 살상을 막으려 했다고 하면 그럴듯해.”
 48|
 49|“놈!”
 50|
 51|“너무 뭐라 하진 마. 나도 이렇게 허접한 짓거리를 계획한 건 아니었으니까. 그런데 생각지도 못한 곳에서 일이 꼬였지. 물론 거기에는…….”
 52|
 53|문득 청년의 시선이 나를 향했다.
 54|
 55|“산서잠룡 진태경. 너도 한몫했고.”
 56|
 57|시선을 마주하는 것만으로도 몸이 굳는 듯했다.
 58|
 59|놈을 향한 적개심 때문인지, 감히 대적할 수 없는 힘의 차이를 느꼈기 때문인지는 모르겠다.
 60|
 61|‘어쩌면 둘 다일 수도.’
 62|
 63|나는 입술을 깨물며 청년을 노려봤다.
 64|
 65|“그게 무슨 개소리지?”
 66|
 67|“네 녀석이 갑자기 비무에 끼어드는 바람에 계획을 하루 앞당겨야 했거든. 그중 가장 큰 변수는 상승검 종리추, 그놈이었고.”
 68|
 69|“……!”
 70|
 71|이것으로 확실해졌다. 종리추는 진범은커녕 공범도 아니었다는 것이.
 72|
 73|“뭐, 결국은 모두 깔끔하게 해결됐지만.”
 74|
 75|놈이 씩 웃으며 손을 내밀었다. 무엇을 원하는지 깨달은 한수가 황급히 한 물건을 내밀었다.
 76|
 77|“소림의 신물, 녹옥불장이오.”
 78|
 79|“그렇군, 이것이 바로…….”
 80|
 81|길쭉한 손가락이 은은하게 빛나는 녹옥불장을 천천히 쓸었다.
 82|
 83|그러나 다음 순간, 청년은 한수의 얼굴을 물끄러미 응시했다. 아직 녹옥불장을 놓지 않은 그의 주름진 손 때문이었다.
 84|
 85|“이젠 놔도 되는데.”
 86|
 87|침을 꿀꺽 삼킨 한수가 대답했다.
 88|
 89|“혀, 혈주께 한 가지 청이 있소.”
 90|
 91|“청이라. 뭐든 말해 보세요. 고생했으니 내 성심성의껏 들어줘야지.”
 92|
 93|이상하다 못해 괴상한 광경이다. 최소 손자뻘은 될 법한 청년에게 설설 기는 노인이라니.
 94|
 95|그 노인이 소림사를 피바다로 만든 천하의 대마두라면 더더욱 그렇다.
 96|
 97|‘도대체 놈의 정체가 뭐지?’
 98|
 99|둘 중 하나다. 암천 내에서 신분이 어마어마하게 높거나, 보이는 것 이상으로 나이가 많거나. 둘 다 맞을 가능성도 충분하다.
100|
101|어쨌건 청년, 혈주라 불린 그의 대답에 한수의 표정이 밝아졌다.
102|
103|“저, 정말이오?”
104|
105|혈주가 혀를 찼다.
106|
107|“속고만 사셨나. 임무를 훌륭히 완수했으니 보상은 당연하지. 한데 얼마나 어려운 부탁을 하려고 우리 음귀 선배님께서 이렇게 뜸을 들이실까?”
108|
109|“그리 어려운 부탁은 아니오.”
110|
111|“하지만 직접 하기에는 어렵고?”
112|
113|“……부끄럽지만 그렇소.”
114|
115|“아하, 뭔지 대충 감 잡았다.”
116|
117|혈주가 나와 적천강을 향해 턱짓했다.
118|
119|“저 두 사람 죽여 달라. 이거잖아, 지금? 맞습니까?”
120|
121|한수가 살기 어린 눈빛으로 고개를 끄덕이자 혈주가 피식 웃었다.
122|
123|“이야, 이건 뜻밖인데? 생각 이상으로 끈끈하셨나 봐.”
124|
125|“자그마치 반평생을 붙어 있던 놈이오. 이 정도는 해 줘야 성에 찰 것 같소.”
126|
127|“의리라…… 뭐, 그것도 좋지.”
128|
129|“최대한 잔인하게 죽여 주시오. 나도 한 손 거들지.”
130|
131|“그걸로 되겠어요? 곧 정파 놈들 몰려오면 골치 아파져. 빨리 끝내고 가려면 선배님도 땀 몇 방울 정도는 흘려야지.”
132|
133|“그럼?”
134|
135|“선배님은 산서잠룡. 나는 화왕. 늦어도 일다경이면 마무리될 것 같은데?”
136|
137|“저 어린놈을 내가? 으하하! 좋소!”
138|
139|나와 적천강의 목숨을 주머니 안의 물건처럼 생각하는 두 놈의 대화에 어처구니가 없었고, 한편으로는 등골이 서늘해졌다.
140|
141|‘저 말…… 진심이다.’
142|
143|일다경. 차 한 잔 마실 짧은 시간에 화왕 적천강을 죽일 수 있다고 단언했다.
144|
145|딱딱하게 굳어 버린 적천강의 표정은 놈의 말이 단순한 허언이 아니라는 증거였다.
146|
147|- 상황의 여의치 않다면 도망쳐라.
148|
149|순간 귓가에 와닿는 전음에 미세하게 고개를 저었다.
150|
151|이미 위에서도 치열한 혈전이 벌어지고 있으니 소림사의 도움은 기대하기 어렵다.
152|
153|만약 내가 발을 뺀다면 적천강은 초절정 고수 두 사람의 집중 공세를 받을 수밖에 없다.
154|
155|‘여기서 마지막까지 버티는 것이 최선이다.’
156|
157|적천강도 그 사실을 안다. 그런데도 이리 말하는 것은…… 그가 남들이 생각하는 것 이상으로 따뜻하고 걱정이 많은 사람이기 때문이다.
158|
159|‘이거, 이번에는 진짜 위험하겠는데.’
160|
161|바짝 마른 입술을 핥으며 백염을 꽉 움켜쥐었다. 그런 내 모습을 본 한수가 비웃었다.
162|
163|“가소로운 놈. 그런다고 무엇이 달라지겠느냐? 네놈의 성취는 제법이다만, 그 정도로는 죽었다 깨어나도 노부를 당해 낼 수 없느니라.”
164|
165|“좆 까세요.”
166|
167|나는 보란 듯이 가래를 탁 뱉었다.
168|
169|“여기 시간으로 몇 시진 정도만 푹 자고 깨어나면 넌 내 손에 죽을걸?”
170|
171|“그게 무슨 개소리냐?”
172|
173|“못 믿겠으면 시험해 보든가.”
174|
175|“이 새파란 애송이가 감히!”
176|
177|안타까울 따름이다. 전투 중이 아니었다면, 로그아웃 시 시간이 느리게 흐르는 대신 완전히 멈춘다면 무한한 시간을 이용해 이 위기에서 벗어날 수 있을 텐데.
178|
179|하지만 지금 생각하는 것들은 모두 개인적인 욕심이다.
180|
181|지금은 망상이 아니라 현실을 마주할 때였다.
182|
183|“산 채로 얼려 주마.”
184|
185|저벅. 저벅. 쩌저적.
186|
187|저 염병할 늙은이의 별호가 어째서 음귀(陰鬼)인지 이제야 똑똑히 알 것 같다.
188|
189|그가 옮기는 발걸음마다 지면이 얼어붙고 나뭇가지에 서리가 내려앉았다.
190|
191|“지독한 음한지기(陰寒地氣)로군. 하나…….”
192|
193|적천강이 내 앞을 가로막았다.
194|
195|“네놈 따위가 감히 노부의 제자를 건드릴 수는 없지.”
196|
197|화아아악!
198|
199|한수의 음한지기가 빙산이라면 적천강의 열양지기는 태양이다.
200|
201|앞서 죽은 염호와 한수의 무공이 대등하다고 가정했을 때, 적천강의 압승은 너무도 당연했다.
202|
203|그러나 한수의 표정은 여유로웠다. 자신의 뒤에 호랑이가 있음을 알기 때문이다.
204|
205|“혈주께서 나서 주셔야겠소.”
206|
207|“아, 그럼요. 슬슬 시작해야지.”
208|
209|녹옥불장을 보물처럼 품에 넣은 혈주가 움직였다. 아니, 사라졌다.
210|
211|그리고 다음 순간.
212|
213|서걱! 툭!
214|
215|소름 끼치는 소리와 함께 튕겨 나온 둥그런 물체가 발치에서 멈췄다.
216|
217|하얗게 센 머리와 점잖아 보이는 용모. 입가에는 채 지워 내지 못한 여유로운 미소가 매달려 있었다.
218|
219|“……!”
220|
221|“……!”
222|
223|나와 적천강은 동시에 눈을 부릅떴다.
224|
225|흉명이 자자한 대마두이자 초절정 고수인 음귀 한수가 단 일격에 목이 날아갔다.
226|
227|그것도 철석같이 믿었던 아군의 손에.
228|
229|경악하는 우리와 달리, 이 모든 일의 주범인 혈주는 태연하기 그지없었다.
230|
231|“개 같은 늙은이. 이래서 근본 없는 것들은 거두면 안 된다니까.”
232|
233|혀를 찬 그는 목 없는 시체가 되어 버린 한수의 몸뚱어리를 슬쩍 밀었다.
234|
235|촤아악. 고목나무처럼 쓰러지는 신형에서 뿜어진 피 분수가 지면을 적셨다.
236|
237|“칼이면 칼답게. 잡은 사람이 휘두르는 대로 갈 것이지. 어딜 감히……!”
238|
239|퍽! 퍽! 우지직!
240|
241|공력을 실은 발길질에 살이 찢기고 뼈가 부서졌다.
242|
243|이미 생기가 빠져나간 한수의 시체를 몇 번이나 밟고 으깨던 혈주가 흘러내린 머리카락을 위로 쓸어올렸다.
244|
245|“꼭 분수를 모르는 것들이 있어요. 자기 수준이 어느 정도인지, 어디까지 나서야 하는지를 몰라. 산서잠룡, 자네도 그렇게 생각하지?”
246|
247|……나?
248|
249|무슨 말을 해야 하나. 나는 머뭇거리다가 솔직히 대답했다.
250|
251|“아니. 그냥 네가 미친 새끼로 보이는데.”
252|
253|잠시 멍하니 나를 바라보던 혈주의 입가에 웃음이 번졌다.
254|
255|“어린놈이 당돌하네.”
256|
257|“넌 아직 어린놈이 벌써부터 좀, 맛이 간 것 같은데.”
258|
259|“어리게 봐 준 건 고맙다. 내가 생각보다 나이가 있거든.”
260|
261|“많아 봤자지.”
262|
263|“아서라. 최소한 네가 지금까지 살아온 인생의 두 배는 살았다.”
264|
265|나는 불신의 눈빛으로 놈을 위아래로 훑었다.
266|
267|나와 엇비슷한 눈높이에 극도로 균형 잡힌 몸.
268|
269|얼굴은 기껏해야 이십 대 초중반의 애송이로밖에 보이지 않는다.
270|
271|이 정도는 단순히 동안이라는 단어로 설명할 수 없다. 하지만 무슨 일이든 벌어질 수 있는 곳이 바로 무림 아닌가.
272|
273|“왜, 생각보다 너무 많아서 놀랐나?”
274|
275|나는 고개를 저었다.
276|
277|“아니. 네 말이 사실이라면 나잇값 못 하는 새끼라고 생각하고 있었지.”
278|
279|“으하하하!”
280|
281|혈주는 유쾌한 웃음을 터트렸다. 하는 행동, 말투. 가볍다 못해 경박하다. 그래서 더 위험하게 느껴진다.
282|
283|놈이 웃느라 허리를 숙이고 있는 지금도 빈틈이 보이지 않았다.
284|
285|어깨까지 들썩이며 웃는 놈의 모습을 노려보던 적천강이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
286|
287|“후회할 게다.”
288|
289|“후회?”
290|
291|웃음을 그친 혈주가 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
292|
293|“내가 왜 후회를 해?”
294|
295|“확실하게 끝내고 싶었다면 음귀를 죽이지 말았어야지.”
296|
297|“어차피 녹슨 칼이야. 효용성이 다했으니 폐기하는 건 당연하지.”
298|

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Han Su—the infamous demonic fiend and Supreme Peak master known as the Yin Ghost—had been beheaded in a single strike.

[P129]
By the ally he had trusted without question.

[P130]
Unlike us, the Blood Lord—the one responsible for everything—remained perfectly calm.

[P131]
“Fucking old man. This is why you should never take in rootless trash.”

[P132]
Clicking his tongue, he casually nudged Han Su’s headless body.

[P133]
Splash!

[P134]
The corpse toppled like a dead tree, spraying a fountain of blood across the ground.

[P135]
“If you’re a sword, act like one. Cut wherever your wielder points you. How dare you…!”

[P136]
Thud! Thud! Crack!

[P137]
His kicks, loaded with internal energy, tore through flesh and shattered bone.

[P138]
After repeatedly stamping and grinding Han Su’s lifeless corpse beneath his feet, the Blood Lord swept his fallen hair back.

[P139]
“There are always people who don’t know their place. They don’t know their own level or when they should stay out of things. Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, don’t you agree?”

[P140]
*…Me?*

[P141]
What was I supposed to say?

[P142]
I hesitated, then answered honestly.

[P143]
“No. You just look like a crazy bastard to me.”

[P144]
For a moment, the Blood Lord stared blankly at me.

[P145]
Then a smile spread across his lips.

[P146]
“You’re bold for a young one.”

[P147]
“You’re still young yourself, and you already seem a little unhinged.”

[P148]
“Thank you for thinking I’m young. I’m older than I look.”

[P149]
“How old could you possibly be?”

[P150]
“Don’t be so sure. I’ve lived at least twice as long as you have.”

[P151]
I looked him up and down in disbelief.

[P152]
He stood at roughly my eye level, his body perfectly proportioned.

[P153]
His face made him look like some inexperienced young man in his early to mid-twenties at most.

[P154]
This went far beyond merely looking young.

[P155]
But if there was anywhere something like this could happen, it was the Murim.

[P156]
“What? Surprised I’m so much older than you expected?”

[P157]
I shook my head.

[P158]
“No. If that’s true, I was thinking you’re a bastard who really doesn’t act his age.”

[P159]
“Wahahaha!”

[P160]
The Blood Lord burst into cheerful laughter.

[P161]
His behavior, his tone—everything about him was light, almost frivolous.

[P162]
That only made him feel more dangerous.

[P163]
Even now, bent over with laughter and his shoulders shaking, he showed not the slightest opening.

[P164]
Jeok Cheongang glared at him before abruptly speaking.

[P165]
“You will regret this.”

[P166]
“Regret?”

[P167]
The Blood Lord stopped laughing and frowned.

[P168]
“Why would I regret it?”

[P169]
“If you wanted to finish this cleanly, you should not have killed the Yin Ghost.”

[P170]
“He was a rusty sword. His usefulness had run out, so disposing of him was only natural.”

[P171]
“A Supreme Peak master is a rusty sword… Then what does that make this old man?”

[P172]
The Blood Lord stroked his chin.

[P173]
“You’re worth rating highly, Fire King. If the Great Faction War had continued for one more year, you probably would have become one of the Four Saints instead of the Three Saints.”

[P174]
“Then it seems my edge has not gone dull yet.”

[P175]
“You’re more than worthy of being called a fine sword.”

[P176]
“What would happen if that fine sword pierced your heart?”

[P177]
“Who knows… I’m sturdier than I look. I doubt that would draw even a single drop of blood.”

[P178]
“When Hong Dao died, this old man swore to heaven.”

[P179]
The Blood Lord smiled faintly as Jeok Cheongang’s gaze grew dark and still.

[P180]
“Even if his killer were a demon god rather than a human, I would see this vengeance through to the end.”

[P181]
“That’s touching and all, but…”

[P182]
The Blood Lord’s smile vanished as he caressed the hilt of the sword at his waist.

[P183]
“I have a feeling the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage will end today.”

[P184]
Without taking his eyes off the Blood Lord, Jeok Cheongang asked me:

[P185]
“What do you think of that?”

[P186]
“I think his mouth needs circumcising. It’s been spewing dick nonstop.”

[P187]
The smile disappeared from the Blood Lord’s face.

[P188]
“……You really are an interesting bastard.”

[P189]
Step.

[P190]
The Blood Lord took one step toward Jeok Cheongang and me, then suddenly spoke.

[P191]
“But how long does that little rat over there plan to keep hiding?”

[P192]
Rustle.

[P193]
A suspicious-looking figure emerged from the distant grass and scratched the back of his head.

[P194]
“Benefactor. I’m sorry. I’ve never been this frightened in my life…”

[P195]
I had never been so happy to see Cheongpung.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P17]
The young man smiled faintly at Jeok Cheongang and nodded.

[P18]
“I told you, didn’t I? It was much easier than I expected. I told him I was going to set off a Heaven-Shaking Thunder in the spectator stands, and he followed me without a fuss.”[^1]

[P19]
“Heaven-Shaking Thunder? Had you planted explosives?”

[P20]
“Ah, that? Of course it was a lie.”

[P21]
“……What?”

[P22]
“Why do people lie? Because every now and then, some idiot falls for it.”

[P23]
Blood dripped from Jeok Cheongang’s fist as he clenched it tight enough to crush bone.

[P24]
“He wasn’t fooled. He allowed himself to be fooled. That was the kind of man Hong Dao was.”

[P26]
“You bastard!”

The young man’s gaze shifted toward me.

[P32]
*Maybe both.*

[P33]
I bit my lip and glared at the young man.

[P34]
“What the fuck are you talking about?”

[P35]

[P36]
“……!”

[P38]

[P39]

[P41]

[P43]
“So this is the…”

[P45]
But the next moment, he stared intently at Han Su’s face.

Han Su’s wrinkled hand was still gripping the staff.

[P47]
“You can let go now.”

[P49]

[P50]

[P51]
It was a strange sight—no, a bizarre one.

[P52]
An old man groveling before a young man who looked young enough to be his grandson.

[P53]
Even more so when that old man was the infamous demonic fiend who had turned Shaolin Temple into a river of blood.

[P54]
*Who the hell is that bastard?*

[P55]
There were only two possibilities.

[P56]
Either his status within Dark Heaven was unimaginably high, or he was much older than he looked.

[P57]
There was also a good chance that both were true.

[P58]
Whatever the case, Han Su’s face brightened at the answer from the young man called the Blood Lord.

[P59]
“R-Really?”

[P60]
The Blood Lord clicked his tongue.

[P61]
“Have you spent your whole life being deceived? You completed your mission perfectly, so a reward is only natural. But what kind of difficult request has our Senior Yin Ghost hesitating like this?”

[P62]
“It is not that difficult a request.”

[P63]
“But it’s difficult for you to handle yourself?”

[P64]
“……I am ashamed to admit it, but yes.”

[P65]
“Ah. I think I know what it is.”

[P66]
The Blood Lord jerked his chin toward Jeok Cheongang and me.

[P67]
“You want me to kill those two, don’t you? Am I right?”

[P68]
Han Su nodded, his eyes filled with killing intent.

[P69]
The Blood Lord let out a short laugh.

[P70]
“Well, this is unexpected. I suppose the two of you were closer than I thought.”

[P71]
“He was at my side for half my life. Nothing less will satisfy me.”

[P72]
“Loyalty… Well, that’s admirable in its own way.”

[P73]
“Kill them as cruelly as possible. I will lend a hand.”

[P74]

[P75]
“Then?”

[P76]

[P77]
“You want me to take that young brat? Wahahaha! Very well!”

[P78]
Their conversation was absurd. They spoke of our lives as though they were objects already tucked inside their pockets.

[P79]
At the same time, a chill ran down my spine.

[P80]
*He means every word.*

[P81]
The Blood Lord had just declared that he could kill the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, within the time it took to drink a cup of tea.

[P82]
The way Jeok Cheongang’s face had stiffened proved that his words were no empty boast.

[P83]
—If things turn against us, run.

[P84]
At the Sound Transmission that suddenly reached my ear, I gave the slightest shake of my head.

[P85]

[P86]
If I pulled out, Jeok Cheongang would have no choice but to face the combined assault of two Supreme Peak masters.

[P87]
*Our best option is to hold out here until the very end.*

[P88]
Jeok Cheongang knew that too.

[P89]
And yet he had told me to run because he was warmer and worried more than anyone realized.

[P90]
*This time, we might really be in trouble.*

[P91]
I licked my parched lips and tightened my grip on White Flame.

[P92]
Han Su sneered at the sight.

[P93]
“Pathetic fool. Do you think that will change anything? Your attainment is impressive enough, but even if you died and came back to life, you could never defeat this old man.”

[P94]
“Go fuck yourself.”

[P95]
I spat a wad of phlegm onto the ground where he could see it.

[P96]
“Give me a few shichen of solid sleep in this world, and when I wake up, you’ll die by my hand.”

[P97]
“What kind of bullshit is that?”

[P98]
“If you don’t believe me, put it to the test.”

[P99]
“How dare you, you green little brat!”

[P100]
It was a damn shame.

[P101]
If I hadn’t been in the middle of a battle, and if time stopped completely when I used Logout instead of merely slowing down, I could have used all the time in the world to escape this crisis.

[P102]
But that was nothing more than wishful thinking.

[P103]
Now was the time to face reality, not indulge in fantasies.

[P104]
“I’ll freeze you alive.”

[P105]
Step. Step. Crack.

[P106]
Now I understood exactly why that damned old man was called the Yin Ghost.

[P107]
The ground froze beneath every step he took, and frost settled over the branches.

[P108]
“What vicious Yin-Cold Qi. But…”

[P109]
Jeok Cheongang stepped in front of me.

[P110]
“A bastard like you will not lay a hand on my Disciple.”

[P111]
Whoosh!

[P112]
If Han Su’s Yin-Cold Qi was an iceberg, Jeok Cheongang’s Scorching Yang Qi was the sun.

[P113]
Assuming Flame Tiger and Han Su were equals in martial prowess, Jeok Cheongang’s overwhelming victory had been inevitable.

[P114]
But Han Su looked perfectly at ease.

[P115]
He knew there was a tiger behind him.

[P116]
“Blood Lord, I will need you to step in.”

[P117]
“Of course. It’s about time we got started.”

[P118]
The Blood Lord tucked the Green Jade Buddha Staff into his robes as carefully as a priceless treasure.

[P119]
Then he moved.

[P120]
No—he vanished.

[P121]
And in the next instant—

[P122]
Slash! Thump!

[P123]
A round object flew through the air with a sickening sound and rolled to a stop at my feet.

[P124]
White hair. Dignified features. A faint smile still lingering around the mouth.

[P125]
“……!”

[P126]
“……!”

[P127]
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened along with mine.

[P128]
Han Su—the infamous demonic fiend and Supreme Peak master known as the Yin Ghost—had been beheaded in a single strike.

[P129]
By the ally he had trusted without question.

[P130]
Unlike us, the Blood Lord—the one responsible for everything—remained perfectly calm.

[P131]
“Fucking old man. This is why you should never take in rootless trash.”

[P132]
Clicking his tongue, he casually nudged Han Su’s headless body.

[P133]
Splash!

[P134]
The corpse toppled like a dead tree, spraying a fountain of blood across the ground.

[P135]
“If you’re a sword, act like one. Cut wherever your wielder points you. How dare you…!”

[P136]
Thud! Thud! Crack!

[P137]
His kicks, loaded with internal energy, tore through flesh and shattered bone.

[P138]
After repeatedly stamping and grinding Han Su’s lifeless corpse beneath his feet, the Blood Lord swept his fallen hair back.

[P139]
“There are always people who don’t know their place. They don’t know their own level or when they should stay out of things. Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, don’t you agree?”

[P140]
*…Me?*

[P141]
What was I supposed to say?

[P142]
I hesitated, then answered honestly.

[P143]
“No. You just look like a crazy bastard to me.”

[P144]
For a moment, the Blood Lord stared blankly at me.

[P145]
Then a smile spread across his lips.

[P146]
“You’re bold for a young one.”

[P147]
“You’re still young yourself, and you already seem a little unhinged.”

[P148]
“Thank you for thinking I’m young. I’m older than I look.”

[P149]
“How old could you possibly be?”

[P150]
“Don’t be so sure. I’ve lived at least twice as long as you have.”

[P151]
I looked him up and down in disbelief.

[P152]
He stood at roughly my eye level, his body perfectly proportioned.

[P153]
His face made him look like some inexperienced young man in his early to mid-twenties at most.

[P154]
This went far beyond merely looking young.

[P155]
But if there was anywhere something like this could happen, it was the Murim.

[P156]
“What? Surprised I’m so much older than you expected?”

[P157]
I shook my head.

[P158]
“No. If that’s true, I was thinking you’re a bastard who really doesn’t act his age.”

[P159]
“Wahahaha!”

[P160]
The Blood Lord burst into cheerful laughter.

[P161]
His behavior, his tone—everything about him was light, almost frivolous.

[P162]
That only made him feel more dangerous.

[P163]
Even now, bent over with laughter and his shoulders shaking, he showed not the slightest opening.

[P164]
Jeok Cheongang glared at him before abruptly speaking.

[P165]
“You will regret this.”

[P166]
“Regret?”

[P167]
The Blood Lord stopped laughing and frowned.

[P168]
“Why would I regret it?”

[P169]
“If you wanted to finish this cleanly, you should not have killed the Yin Ghost.”

[P170]
“He was a rusty sword. His usefulness had run out, so disposing of him was only natural.”

[P171]
“A Supreme Peak master is a rusty sword… Then what does that make this old man?”

[P172]
The Blood Lord stroked his chin.

[P173]
“You’re worth rating highly, Fire King. If the Great Faction War had continued for one more year, you probably would have become one of the Four Saints instead of the Three Saints.”

[P174]
“Then it seems my edge has not gone dull yet.”

[P175]
“You’re more than worthy of being called a fine sword.”

[P176]
“What would happen if that fine sword pierced your heart?”

[P177]
“Who knows… I’m sturdier than I look. I doubt that would draw even a single drop of blood.”

[P178]
“When Hong Dao died, this old man swore to heaven.”

[P179]
The Blood Lord smiled faintly as Jeok Cheongang’s gaze grew dark and still.

[P180]
“Even if his killer were a demon god rather than a human, I would see this vengeance through to the end.”

[P181]
“That’s touching and all, but…”

[P182]
The Blood Lord’s smile vanished as he caressed the hilt of the sword at his waist.

[P183]
“I have a feeling the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage will end today.”

[P184]
Without taking his eyes off the Blood Lord, Jeok Cheongang asked me:

[P185]
“What do you think of that?”

[P186]
“I think his mouth needs circumcising. It’s been spewing dick nonstop.”

[P187]
The smile disappeared from the Blood Lord’s face.

[P188]
“……You really are an interesting bastard.”

[P189]
Step.

[P190]
The Blood Lord took one step toward Jeok Cheongang and me, then suddenly spoke.

[P191]
“But how long does that little rat over there plan to keep hiding?”

[P192]
Rustle.

[P193]
A suspicious-looking figure emerged from the distant grass and scratched the back of his head.

[P194]
“Benefactor. I’m sorry. I’ve never been this frightened in my life…”

[P195]
I had never been so happy to see Cheongpung.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
